concerns.text: FR-001 and US-1 require separate analysis of He/p and Fe/p ratios (implying distinct Helium and Iron flux columns). T015 and T038 mandate a single 'heavy_flux' column in the output schema. A single column cannot support the per-species rigidity-binned correlation and modulation analysis required by FR-003 and FR-004, making the core scientific hypothesis untestable.

FR-007 requires flagging gaps > 30 days and excluding them from *statistical analysis*. The US-1 Independent Test requires the output file to 'contain no missing dates... or explicitly flag gaps' and match 'expected daily resolution'. T013/T049 mandate segmenting the time series and excluding gaps from the *output dataset* entirely. This creates a contradiction where the task's exclusion logic prevents the spec's 'complete daily resolution' test from passing.

FR-006 and US-3 require fitting the rigidity-dependent diffusion model to modulation amplitudes derived from **composition ratios** (He/p, Fe/p) to validate species-dependent transport. T029 instructs the model to use `modulation_amplitudes_baseline.csv` derived from **absolute fluxes** (the control analysis in FR-008). Fitting the physics model to the baseline contradicts the requirement to validate the hypothesis about differential modulation in the ratios.

SC-003 requires measuring the 'width of the 95% confidence interval... against the stability of the correlation coefficient' (e.g., a ratio or threshold comparison). T033 only calculates the width and checks if the interval includes zero (binary check). It fails to implement the mechanism to measure/report the 'width against stability' required by the success criterion.

FR-004 and US-2 Independent Test explicitly require calculating correlations for 'all lags between -12 and +12 months' (implying integer month steps). T019 defines a lag window of '±12 months' but is ambiguous about whether it iterates through every integer lag or just the endpoints, risking a failure to produce the full correlation matrix required by the test.

The spec's Assumptions state the coverage threshold is 'to be defined... based on statistical power analysis' without pre-defining the effect size. T016b hardcodes an 'expected effect size (correlation > 0.3)' in the logic. This conflicts with the 'deferred' nature of the threshold definition if the actual data variance suggests a different effect size, requiring a refactor to make the effect size a true input parameter.

T005 mandates writing JSON-formatted logs to `data/logs/pipeline.log`. This violates Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) which forbids modifying data files in place and requires derivations to produce new files. Logs should be written to a `logs/` directory or stdout/stderr, not mixed into the `data/` artifact hierarchy.
